_comment: Pronunciation lexicon for Video E (narration skill, PRONUNCIATION.md). Only respell and accept change narration; say/ipa/lang/sources/decoy/note/probe are the record. Looked up with lookup_pronunciation.py and probed with probe_names.py run --write in this video's voice, michael (2026-10-12, ftts 0.1.11, FrankenWhisper 0.10.0, 3 carriers, control + decoy). The script speaks two of these names: von Neumann (10_1) and Pascal (06_5). Peres and Elias are on screen only (10_4): their probes did not pass, so a later script that wants them spoken must first find a spelling that does. Not in this file because the video only shows them and no source for the person's own pronunciation was found: Forsythe, Samuelson, Blum, Diaconis, Bartoš, Hoeffding, Dijkstra (the lookup tool guessed Samuelson from German spelling rules, which is wrong for Paul Samuelson). Re-probe when the voice or the ftts version changes; the owner's pronunciation overrides every entry.

results.von Neumann: control UNVERIFIED 0/3 (the ASR wrote 'von Neumann' every time)
results.von NOY-muhn: candidate FAIL 0/3 (heard 'Von N-O-Y Moon', 'Von Neumoon', 'von Neumun'): dropped
results.von Noy-man: candidate UNVERIFIED 0/3 (the ASR wrote 'von Neumann' every time)
results.von NEW-man: decoy FOOLED the ASR in 2 of 3 carriers (written 'von Neumann')

von Neumann.note: English usage, as Wikipedia's lead gives it. The ASR writes the famous name for the right reading and for the wrong one (NEW-man), so it cannot verify this name. Judged instead from spectrograms of the three reads of 'This is von Neumann.' (0 to 3.5 kHz): after the n, the plain spelling and 'von Noy-man' both show the second formant rising (the 'oy' glide), most clearly in the respelling, while the decoy's falls from high to low ('nyoo'). That is a reading of a picture, not a listener's verdict: the plain spelling is listed first, 'von Noy-man' is the alternate, and whoever directs the narration should look at 10_1's take for the same rise.

Pascal.note: Spoken as 'Pascal's triangle' (06_5). English usage; the French is pah-SKAHL. The plain spelling was heard as 'Pascale' and 'Pascoe' in two of three carriers; 'Pa-skal' passed in all three.

results.Peres: control FAIL 0/3 (written 'Peres' twice, 'Paris' once; the written name does not sound like the target to the scorer)

Peres.note: On screen only; not verified for speech. Yuval Peres's article gives no pronunciation; the target is the English usage Wikipedia records for the same Hebrew surname (Shimon Peres), an inference about the name, not his own usage. The lookup tool's first answer (PAY-reess, from the Portuguese surname) is wrong for him and was not kept.

results.Elias: control UNVERIFIED 0/3 (the ASR wrote 'Elias' every time)
results.Ih-ly-us: candidate FAIL 1/3 (one read ran on, repeating itself)

Elias.note: On screen only; not verified for speech. The standard English reading of the name; Peter Elias's own usage was not verified. Hyphenated respellings made michael spell letters or run on; the plain spelling is the only usable one found.
